sample.question:
Tower of Hanoi is a classic puzzle with three pegs labeled A, B and C (left to right) and several disks of different sizes. Disks are numbered by size: disk 1 is the smallest. A disk's number is printed on it. Only the TOP disk of a peg can be moved, and it may only be placed on an empty peg or on top of a LARGER disk. The move X->Y means: take the top disk of peg X and put it on peg Y.

You want to gather all 3 disks on peg C in as few moves as possible. Starting from the position in the image, which move should you make FIRST? Exactly one of the moves below starts an optimal solution.

Options:
[1] A->B
[2] A->C
[3] B->A
[4] B->C
[5] C->A
[6] C->B
sample.analysis:
Initial position: peg A: empty; peg B: disks [3, 2, 1] (bottom to top); peg C: empty. A breadth-first search shows the optimum from here is 7 moves.
Evaluate every possible first move:
A->B: illegal (peg A is empty).
A->C: illegal (peg A is empty).
B->A: legal; after it, the remaining optimum is 7 moves, total 1 + 7 = 8.
B->C: legal; after it, the remaining optimum is 6 moves, total 1 + 6 = 7. <- optimal
C->A: illegal (peg C is empty).
C->B: illegal (peg C is empty).
Only B->C keeps the total at 7 moves, so it is the unique optimal first move. The option number is 4.
